articles.summary: Transaction strengthens balance sheet with pre-tax cash proceeds of approximately $1.45 billion, before customary closing adjustments HOUSTON and LONDON, Nov. 02, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) - Baker Hughes (NASDAQ: BKR, “the Company”), an energy technology company, announced Monday the successful sale of its Waygate Technologies business to Hexagon. The all-cash transaction is valued at approximately $1.45 billion, before customary closing adjustments. The sale encompasses Waygate Technologies’ remote visual inspection, ultrasound, radiography, and imaging solutions portfolios, and all assets of the business, including intellectual property, footprint and resources. This divestiture reinforces the Company’s commitment to disciplined portfolio management, enhances the durability of earnings and cash flow, and further strengthens the Company’s balance sheet. articles.summary: HOUSTON and LONDON, Nov. 19, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) - Baker Hughes (NASDAQ: BKR), an energy technology company, in consortium with McDermott, has been awarded a contract by INPEX for the next phase of the Ichthys liquefied natural gas (LNG) development offshore Western Australia. The contract was awarded under the consortium’s existing Subsea Development Framework Agreement with INPEX. It covers the engineering, procurement, construction, installation (EPCI) and commissioning of new subsea infrastructure that will tie back to the existing Ichthys offshore production system. articles.title: INPEX Awards McDermott-Baker Hughes Consortium Contract for Ichthys LNG Development

articles.summary: Agreement includes roadmap for evaluating and developing next-generation enhanced geothermal systems (EGS) nationwide Supports Türkiye’s dual ambitions to reduce emissions and strengthen domestic energy security ANTALYA, Türkiye, Nov. 12, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) - Baker Hughes (NASDAQ: BKR), an energy technology company, and Türkiye Petrolleri Anonim Ortaklığı (TPAO) announced Thursday an agreement to explore opportunities for enhanced geothermal systems (EGS), supporting Türkiye’s ambitions to scale lower carbon geothermal power generation and strengthen energy security. The agreement was signed during COP 31, the United Nations’ flagship climate conference, which is taking place this week in Antalya, Türkiye. The agreement outlines a phased approach for industrializing next-generation geothermal development, which includes a country-wide assessment to evaluate EGS potential using data from TPAO and the General Directorate of Mineral Research and Exploration (MTA).
